chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon them, who said:
I said to him: “What is your rank, and whom do you resemble among those who passed before?” He said: “The companion of Mūsā and Dhū al-Qarnayn; both were knowledgeable, and they were not Prophets.”

key_terms.تُشْبِهُونَ: you resemble or are similar to
key_terms.ذُو الْقَرْنَيْنِ: Dhū al-Qarnayn, an earlier figure known for special knowledge and authority
key_terms.صَاحِبُ مُوسَى: the companion of Mūsā عليه السلام, cited as a past parallel
key_terms.عَالِمَيْنِ: two knowledgeable ones, possessing divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.نَبِيَّيْنِ: two Prophets; here used in negation to distinguish knowledge from prophethood

ai.seo_question: How do the Imams عليهم السلام compare to righteous figures of the past without being Prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the station of the Imams عليهم السلام by comparing them to exemplary figures from earlier communities who possessed divinely granted knowledge without being Prophets. It highlights a distinction between profound sacred knowledge and prophethood, affirming elevated religious authority without claiming nubuwwah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are your (Imams<sup>asws</sup>) positions, and who resembles you from the ones of the past?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Companion of Musa<sup>as</sup>, and Zul Qarnayn were both knowledgeable ones, and they did not happen to be Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ’Udhayna from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiya who has said that he asked abu Ja‘far and abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) the following.
“What is your position? To who of the people of the past do you resemble?” the Imam (a.s.) said, “I resemble the companion of Moses and Dhul Qarnayn who were two scholars but not two prophets.”
